value_stream.name: Merchandise Financial Planning, Open-to-Buy & Margin Management

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Merchandise Planners, Category Managers, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), CFO
fields.Trigger: Annual corporate planning cycle (links to VS-33.1)

workflows.name: Annual Merchandise Financial Plan & Sales/Margin Budget Development

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Category Managers build the bottom-up plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "FP&A/CFO approve the annual merchandise financial plan, lock the" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-532 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Merchandise Financial Planning & Open-to-Buy (PA-101.1).)
- operational: OTB change-authority matrix enforced in-system with SLA-tracked approvals; in-season reforecast per W3288
Pain Points / Risks: - **Top-down/bottom-up mismatch risk**: Unrealistic corporate targets force overbuy or margin sacrifice; mitigated by structured reconciliation and scenario modeling (W3296)
- **Assumption-staleness risk**: Locked annual assumptions drift from reality; mitigated by in-season reforecast (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise financial planning / OTB module; FP&A/budgeting (links to VS-17.4); BI planning (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planners receive the corporate revenue and gross-margin target from FP&A (links to VS-33.1 annual business plan) and decompose it into a top-down merchandise financial plan: total sales, gross-margin %, GM$ , beginning/ending inventory, and receipt budget by month and by department

Category Managers build the bottom-up plan: prior-year actuals, known events (new stores per VS-37, store closures per VS-59, promo calendar per VS-14.1, seasonal calendar per profile §13.2), price/mix changes, and private-label growth (links to VS-41); reconcile top-down to bottom-up and resolve gaps

FP&A/CFO approve the annual merchandise financial plan, lock the IMU/markdown assumptions (W3286), set the OTB envelope (W3283), and feed the plan into the merchandising and finance systems; establish monthly P&A review cadence (W3288) and variance thresholds

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Buyers (links to VS-03), Allocation (links to VS-55)
fields.Trigger: Season boundary (per profile §13.2: summer/dry, rainy-season/flood-control, ber-months/Christmas)

workflows.name: Seasonal Merchandise Plan & Department/Category Financial Plan

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Category Managers translate the seasonal financial plan into a" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "Merchandise Planner lock the seasonal plan, allocate OTB to" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-532 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Merchandise Financial Planning & Open-to-Buy (PA-101.1).)
- operational: early season planning and import pipeline visibility; operational: OTB discipline (W3283) and reforecast (W3288)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Season-timing risk**: Late seasonal plan misses import lead times (45–90 days per VS-02.2); mitigated by early season planning and import pipeline visibility
- **Over/under-stock risk**: Poor seasonal depth planning causes clearance loss or lost sales; mitigated by OTB discipline (W3283) and reforecast (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning / assortment planning (links to VS-01.1); allocation (links to VS-55); seasonal clearance (links to VS-64)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner develop the seasonal merchandise plan by department/category: seasonal sales, GM%, planned receipts, BOM/EOM stock, weeks-of-supply (W3289), and markdown budget (W3285); incorporate seasonal-calendar events and prior-season actuals (links to VS-64 seasonal transition)

Category Managers translate the seasonal financial plan into a category plan: key items (links to VS-01.1 assortment), depth/width, launch/clearance timing, promo tie-ins (links to VS-14.1/VS-58), and import-vs-domestic mix (links to VS-02.2/VS-87); commit the buy against OTB (W3283/W3284)

Merchandise Planner lock the seasonal plan, allocate OTB to categories, and publish the seasonal scorecard baseline for in-season tracking (W3288); coordinate launch readiness with allocation and stores

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Buyers (links to VS-03), VP Merchandising, FP&A (links to VS-17.4)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-calculate of "calculate OTB per department/category" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Buyers consume OTB by raising POs/blanket releases" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report OTB utilization to VP Merchandising and FP&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-69 (ensure merchandise financial plan & OTB discipline.)
- operational: hard OTB controls and weekly recalculation; operational: reforecast-driven OTB release (W3288)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-buy risk**: Buying ahead of OTB inflates inventory and erodes turn (W3290); mitigated by hard OTB controls and weekly recalculation
- **Under-buy risk**: Over-tight OTB causes lost sales on trending items; mitigated by reforecast-driven OTB release (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - OTB / merchandise planning module; PO/open-order (links to VS-03.2); in-transit import (links to VS-02.2); markdown (links to VS-64)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner calculate OTB per department/category: planned EOM stock + planned sales + planned markdowns − stock-on-hand − on-order (open POs per VS-03.2 and in-transit import per VS-02.2); the residual is the available-to-buy dollars for the period

Buyers consume OTB by raising POs/blanket releases (links to VS-03.2) within available OTB; system blocks or warns on over-buy; Merchandise Planner release additional OTB only with VP Merchandising approval and documented rationale

Merchandise Planner recalculate OTB weekly using latest actuals (sales, receipts, markdowns) and reforecast (W3288); adjust forward commitments, cancel/defer open orders where indicated, and report OTB utilization to VP Merchandising and FP&A

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Buyers (links to VS-03), Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), Import (links to VS-02.2)

workflows.name: Category & Sub-Class Receipt Planning & Commitment Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Merchandise Planner/Buyers convert OTB into a category and sub-class" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track committed vs received" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Merchandise Planner track receipt commitments against OTB and plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-69 (ensure merchandise financial plan & OTB discipline.)
- operational: pipeline tracking (links to VS-02); operational: OTB controls (W3283)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Timing-slip risk**: Import delays cause receipt-plan gaps and lost sales; mitigated by pipeline tracking (links to VS-02.2 W728) and reforecast (W3288)
- **Over-commit risk**: Committing beyond OTB erodes inventory turn; mitigated by OTB controls (W3283)
System Touchpoints: - Receipt/commitment planning; PO (links to VS-03.2); import/in-transit (links to VS-02.2); allocation (links to VS-55)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/Buyers convert OTB into a category and sub-class receipt plan: receipt dollars and units by month/week, split by domestic (7–21-day lead) vs import (45–90-day lead per VS-02.2/VS-87), and key-item level for A-items

Buyers commit the receipt plan via PO/blanket release (links to VS-03.2) and track committed vs received; coordinate import pipeline and container planning (links to VS-02.2 W1264) and phased delivery for projects (links to VS-77)
Merchandise Planner track receipt commitments against OTB and plan, flag over/under-commit and timing slips, and reconcile to on-order and in-transit; feed exceptions to weekly review (W3288)

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Category Managers, Merchandise Planners, Pricing (links to VS-01.2/VS-57), Finance (links to VS-17.1)
fields.Volume: ~6 seasonal clearance events/year + ongoing slow-mover markdowns

workflows.name: Markdown & Clearance Budget Allocation & Spend Authorization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-allocate of "allocate the markdown budget" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validates against remaining markdown budget" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track markdown spend against budget, compute realized margin impact" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-69 (ensure merchandise financial plan & OTB discipline.)
- operational: budget controls and optimization analytics (W3299); operational: reserve policy and clearance discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-markdown risk**: Excess markdown spend erodes planned margin; mitigated by budget controls and optimization analytics (W3299)
- **Under-markdown risk**: Withholding needed markdowns leaves aged inventory (W3294) and ties up working capital; mitigated by reserve policy and clearance discipline
System Touchpoints: - Markdown management; price management (links to VS-01.2); clearance (links to VS-64); GL margin posting (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/VP Merchandising allocate the markdown budget (markdown $ and %) across departments/categories from the annual plan (W3281); set seasonal clearance envelopes (links to VS-64) and slow-mover/reserve policy (W3294)

Category Managers request markdowns (permanent price reductions, promotional markdowns, clearance) within budget; system validates against remaining markdown budget; VP Merchandising authorizes per authority matrix (links to VS-36); price execution via VS-01.2/VS-08

Merchandise Planner/Finance track markdown spend against budget, compute realized margin impact (W3286), and report markdown variance to FP&A; coordinate clearance execution (links to VS-64.2) and disposition (links to VS-05.3/VS-32.3)

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Pricing (links to VS-01.2/VS-57), FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Rebate (links to VS-39)
fields.Trigger: Annual plan; pricing/cost change; markdown decision

workflows.name: Gross-Margin Plan, Initial Markup (IMU) & Markdown-Margin Modeling

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "import FX impact" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile planned vs actual maintained margin, isolate drivers" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-532 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Merchandise Financial Planning & Open-to-Buy (PA-101.1).)
- operational: pricing analytics (links to VS-57) and margin modeling; operational: P&A variance tracking (W3288)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: Cost inflation not passed through erodes IMU; mitigated by pricing analytics (links to VS-57) and margin modeling
- **Model error risk**: Wrong elasticity/shrink assumptions distort the plan; mitigated by P&A variance tracking (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - Margin/IMU planning; price management (links to VS-01.2); landed cost (links to VS-02.2/VS-87); rebate (links to VS-39); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner set the IMU plan (gross margin before markdown) by category using cost (incl. landed cost per VS-02.2/VS-87), retail, vendor rebates (links to VS-39), and mix; model the maintained margin = IMU − markdown % − shrink (links to VS-23) to hit the 28–32% gross-margin target

Category Managers model price/cost/mix scenarios: vendor cost increase (links to VS-03.3), SRP change (links to VS-01.2), bundle pricing (links to VS-92), promo elasticity (links to VS-58), and import FX impact (links to VS-18.3); select the mix that preserves maintained margin

Merchandise Planner/FP&A reconcile planned vs actual maintained margin, isolate drivers (IMU, markdown, shrink, mix, FX), and feed variance to weekly P&A (W3288) and monthly finance close (links to VS-17.1)

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Ecommerce (links to VS-10/VS-65/VS-95), Category Managers, FP&A (links to VS-17.4)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "account for channel-specific cost" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "catalog content per VS-01.3" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track channel contribution margin" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-532 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Merchandise Financial Planning & Open-to-Buy (PA-101.1).)
- operational: channel contribution analytics and routing (links to VS-60); operational: price-parity governance (links to VS-57)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Channel-cannibalization risk**: Ecommerce growth shifts margin to higher-cost fulfillment; mitigated by channel contribution analytics and routing (links to VS-60)
- **Channel-price-disparity risk**: Inconsistent channel pricing undermines trust; mitigated by price-parity governance (links to VS-57)
System Touchpoints: - Multi-channel planning; ecommerce (links to VS-10); marketplace (links to VS-65/VS-95); order routing (links to VS-60); FP&A (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner allocate the revenue/margin plan across channels: in-store (97.1%), ecommerce BOPIS+delivery (links to VS-10), marketplace presence (links to VS-65), and BuildRight-operated marketplace (links to VS-95); account for channel-specific cost (fulfillment fee per profile §2, last-mile per VS-06/VS-56, marketplace commission)

Category Managers set channel assortment/price strategy (which SKUs on which channel, channel price parity per VS-57, digital-catalog content per VS-01.3) and allocate receipt/OTB to support multi-channel demand (links to VS-60 order routing)

Merchandise Planner/FP&A track channel contribution margin (revenue − COGS − channel fulfillment cost), isolate channel profitability, and re-plan channel mix as ecommerce grows to 5–7% (links to VS-10)

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Merchandise Planners, Category Managers, Buyers, Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), FP&A (links to VS-17.4)

workflows.name: Merchandise Plan-vs-Actual Review, In-Season Forecast & Reforecast

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compile weekly P&A" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "update season-end projection using actuals + remaining weeks" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review with Buyers, Supply Planning, and FP&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-69 (ensure merchandise financial plan & OTB discipline.)
- operational: weekly cadence and key-item decisioning (W3298); operational: clear authority and SLA
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reforecast-latency risk**: Late reaction to in-season trend causes stockouts or overstock; mitigated by weekly cadence and key-item decisioning (W3298)
- **Decision-deferral risk**: Slow markdown/chase decisions lock in margin loss; mitigated by clear authority and SLA
System Touchpoints: - P&A / reforecast module; demand planning (links to VS-02.1); OTB (W3283); BI/dashboard (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner compile weekly P&A: actual vs plan for sales, GM%, receipts, markdowns, EOM stock, sell-through, and weeks-of-supply by department/category/key-item; flag variances beyond threshold

Category Managers/Merchandise Planner reforecast in-season: update season-end projection using actuals + remaining weeks; decide reorder/cancel/markdown actions against OTB (W3283/W3284) and markdown budget (W3285); coordinate supply response (links to VS-02.1)

VP Merchandising conduct weekly P&A review with Buyers, Supply Planning, and FP&A; approve actions (chase, cancel, markdown, transfer per VS-05.2), update OTB and markdown budget, and report material variance to CFO/COO (links to VS-33.2)
